title: 二极管：电流的单行道
summary: 先把二极管故意插反，看 LED 不亮；再转过来。二极管只让电流朝一个方向走，代价是大约 0.65 V。
concepts: anode / cathode 阳极 / 阴极
description: 二极管只让电流从阳极流向阴极（色环那一端）。把它串在电池 + 后面：正接时它导通，只吃掉约 0.65 V；电池接反时它截止，后面的电路一点电流都没有。电路：9 V 电池 + → 二极管 → 470 Ω → 绿色 LED → GND。

cards.title: 故意插反一次
text: **9 V 电池**接上方电源轨。然后搭一串：+ 轨 → **二极管** → **`470 Ω`** → **绿色 LED** → GND。
二极管故意**插反**：让有**色环**的那一端朝 + 轨。
LED 亮吗？再把二极管**掉个头**，看看有什么不同。色环那一端，到底是哪一端？

cards.title: 二极管是一个单向阀
text: - 二极管像水管里的**单向阀**：电流只能从**阳极**流进、从**阴极**（色环端）流出。反过来，阀门关死。
![](fig:iv)
- 正向导通时，它要“收”一小段几乎固定的电压，叫**正向压降**。本仿真把硅二极管当成 0.65 V 再串一个 0.8 Ω 的小电阻：
- 代入数字：就算电流大到 0.1 A，$V_D = 0.65 + 0.8 × 0.1 = 0.73$ V。电流变十倍，压降只多零点几伏——它几乎是个常数。
![](fig:loop)
- 所以把它串在电池后面，就是一道**防反接**保险：接对了只少约 0.65 V，接反了一点电流都过不去。

cards.title: 接对方向，测一测
text: - 二极管**阳极**（没有色环的一端）插 + 轨，**阴极**接 `470 Ω`，电阻接 LED 长脚，LED 短脚接 GND。
- 点**「检查我的电路」**。通过后，用万用表测下面几个电压，再单击 LED 看它的电流。
- 先自己预测：电池 9 V 减去二极管和 LED 两道“坎”，剩下的压在 470 Ω 上。

cards.title: 带走
text: - **二极管是单行道**：电流从阳极流向色环端（阴极）。LED 也是一种二极管，所以它插反了也不亮。
- 正向压降几乎不随电流变：硅二极管约 0.65 V。防反接的代价就是这一小段电压。
- 真实电路里的坑：3.3 V 或一节锂电池供电时，0.65 V 占了电源的一大块。那时改用压降只有约 0.3 V 的**肖特基二极管**——5.2 的开发板在 USB 入口就用了一只。

caption.text: 反向（电压为负）：电流是 0，阀门关死。正向过了约 0.65 V：电流猛涨，电压几乎不再变。

i18n.en: Reverse (negative voltage): no current, the valve is shut. Forward, past about 0.65 V: the current soars while the voltage hardly moves.

caption.text: 电池的 9 V 分成三份：二极管收 V_D，LED 收 V_f，剩下的落在 470 Ω 上。同一个电流 I 穿过全部。

i18n.en: The battery's 9 V splits three ways: the diode takes V_D, the LED V_f, and the rest falls across 470 Ω. One current I passes through all of them.

en.title: Diodes: a one-way street for current
en.summary: Put the diode in backwards on purpose and watch the LED stay dark; then turn it round. A diode lets current go one way only, at a cost of about 0.65 V.
en.description: A diode only lets current flow from its anode to its cathode (the banded end). Put one in series after the battery's +: connected correctly it conducts and takes only about 0.65 V; with the battery reversed it blocks, and no current at all reaches the circuit after it. Circuit: 9 V battery + → diode → 470 Ω → green LED → GND.

cards.title: Put it in backwards once
text: Connect the **9 V battery** to the top rails. Then build a chain: + rail → **diode** → **`470 Ω`** → **green LED** → GND.
Put the diode in **backwards on purpose**: the end with the **band** faces the + rail.
Is the LED lit? Now **turn the diode round** and look again. Which end is the banded one, really?

cards.title: A diode is a one-way valve
text: - A diode is like a **check valve** in a water pipe: current can only go in at the **anode** and out at the **cathode** (the banded end). The other way, the valve is shut.
![](fig:iv)
- Conducting forward, it takes a small, almost fixed slice of voltage: the **forward voltage**. This simulator models a silicon diode as 0.65 V plus a small 0.8 Ω resistance:
- With numbers: even at a large 0.1 A, $V_D = 0.65 + 0.8 × 0.1 = 0.73$ V. Ten times the current adds only a few tenths of a volt — it is almost a constant.
![](fig:loop)
- So a diode in series after the battery is a **reverse-polarity** guard: connected right you lose about 0.65 V; connected wrong, no current gets through at all.

cards.title: The right way round, measured
text: - The diode's **anode** (the end without the band) goes in the + rail, its **cathode** to the `470 Ω`, the resistor to the LED's long lead, the LED's short lead to GND.
- Press **Check my circuit**. Once it passes, measure the voltages below with the multimeter, then click the LED to see its current.
- Predict first: the battery's 9 V minus two "steps" (the diode and the LED); what is left sits across the 470 Ω.

cards.title: Take away
text: - **A diode is a one-way street**: current goes from the anode to the banded end (the cathode). An LED is a diode too, which is why a reversed LED stays dark.
- The forward voltage hardly changes with current: about 0.65 V for silicon. That small slice is the price of reverse protection.

- A real-world catch: on 3.3 V or a single lithium cell, 0.65 V is a big piece of the supply. There a **Schottky diode** is used instead, with only about 0.3 V — the dev board in 5.2 has one on its USB input.

measurements.ask: Multimeter: the diode's banded end (cathode) to GND
measurements.explain: 9 V minus the diode's drop, minus a little across the battery's own 1.5 Ω: about 8.32 V.

measurements.ask: Multimeter: the + rail (the diode's anode) to GND
measurements.explain: Slightly under 9 V: about 13 mA through the battery's 1.5 Ω costs about 0.02 V.

measurements.ask: From your two readings: the diode's forward voltage V_D = anode − cathode
measurements.explain: 0.65 + 0.8 × 0.013 ≈ 0.66 V — just above the 0.65 V knee.

measurements.ask: Click the LED: what current do Properties show?
Now imagine the battery connected backwards, with the diode still the right way round. The LED:
choices: stays dark, and nothing after the diode gets any current
measurements.explain: Reversed, the diode's anode is at − and its cathode at +: the valve is shut. No current flows, so the LED (and any circuit after it) is safe.

hints: Like an LED, a diode has a direction: current flows from the anode into the banded end (the cathode).
The diode's anode can go straight into the red + rail; its banded end goes into a row of holes.
tests: LED on; the diode's cathode one diode drop below the battery

measurements.explain: 9 V 减去二极管的压降，再减去电池自己 1.5 Ω 内阻上的一点点：约 8.32 V。

measurements.explain: 比 9 V 低一点：约 13 mA 流过电池的 1.5 Ω 内阻，掉了约 0.02 V。

measurements.ask: 用你的两个读数算二极管的正向压降：V_D = 阳极 − 阴极
单击 LED：「属性」里显示的电流是多少？
设想电池接反了（二极管方向不变），LED 会？
choices: 不亮，二极管后面的电路一点电流都没有
measurements.explain: 电池反过来，二极管的阳极在 −、阴极在 +，单向阀关死。没有电流，LED 和后面的电路都安全。

hints: 二极管和 LED 一样有方向：电流从阳极流进，从色环端（阴极）流出。
二极管的阳极可以直接插在红色 + 轨上；色环端插进一列孔里。
